source.title: A Unifying Framework for Unsupervised Concept Extraction

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper derives a population identifiability result for a constrained sparse dictionary-learning model. This bears on whether extracted features can be canonical, but it uses theoretical identifiability analysis rather than testing SAE feature recovery empirically.
record.gate_note: The paper's own relevant result is a theorem for spark-constrained sparse dictionary learning. It does not test superposition geometry, interference, sparsity-dependent transitions, feature importance, LLM feature structure, or empirical SAE recovery. Statements about SAE instability and other empirical findings are cited from prior work, not results of this paper.
record.test_reason: This is a pure theory paper. It gives an identifiability meta-theorem for latent concept generative models and uses it to re-derive classic results: spark-constrained dictionary learning (an adaptation of Aharon et al. 2006), linear ICA (Comon 1994) and Gaussian mixtures. It reports no measurement of trained SAEs, toy networks or LLM representations. So none of its own results bears on whether SAE features are stable or canonical units of a model. Claim 5.2 concerns an abstract model class, not a model's representation. The claims that SAEs do not recover canonical features across seeds are cited from Leask et al. and Paulo & Belrose, not shown here. Footnote 5 says the ordinary SAE class lacks the guarantee, but that is a remark about a model class, not a test. The record's 'tests/T2' and its V5 labels are therefore not supported.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors present a framework that casts concept extraction as identifying a latent concept generative model. Their meta-theorem reduces identifiability proofs to intersecting two transition sets, and they show it recovers existing results (dictionary learning, linear ICA, Gaussian mixtures). They stress that guarantees hold only relative to a specified model class, and that standard SAE classes lack the spark-based guarantee without post-hoc checks. The dictionary-learning result is a re-derivation of Aharon et al. (2006), not a new finding.
record.recipe_differences: Uses population identifiability theory and a spark-constrained dictionary-learning model class; it does not reproduce the original toy-network training or geometry measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The stated identifiability result depends on the spark condition σ > 2s and the specified model-class assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Claim 5.2 proves that the population spark-constrained sparse dictionary model (σ > 2s, linear deterministic mixing) is identifiable up to relabeling and scaling. The paper states that the relaxed SAE class Msae lacks this guarantee and proposes post-hoc spark checks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse dictionary models are theoretically identifiable up to permutation and scaling only under extra constraints (e.g. spark > 2s); standard SAE model classes carry no such guarantee.

record.problems: The evidence is theoretical and conditional on a restrictive model class; there are no empirical SAE or LLM experiments, and no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No other relevant own results were reported. Cited claims about SAE instability and other empirical work were excluded.

untested.parts: Entirely untested: no toy models, geometry, interference or sparsity-dependent transition.
Entirely untested: no capacity or feature-importance analysis.
Entirely untested: no analysis of other causes of polysemanticity.
Entirely untested: no LLM activations and no SAE recovery experiments.

Untested empirically: no trained SAEs, no cross-seed stability, no completeness or canonicity measurements. Only a population identifiability theorem for a spark-constrained model class, plus a remark that the plain SAE class lacks it.
Entirely untested: concepts are assumed to be coordinates in R^d; one-dimensional versus multi-dimensional features is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels should be dropped: the only row is a theorem about an abstract model class, not evidence about SAE features of any model. The SAE-instability statements in the introduction are cited prior work. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions, interference, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular superposition geometry.
Does not test capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, or feature sharing.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemanticity or whether polysemanticity indicates superposition.
Does not measure feature distribution across LLM neurons or SAE recovery of sparse features.

The identifiability result is for a specified population model class; the paper does not test learned SAE features, their empirical stability across runs, or whether they are complete units in real models.
Does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Mspk(d, p; s, σ)
rows.operation_detail: Derives population identifiability for a spark-constrained sparse dictionary-learning model class.
rows.measure: Identifiability of the model up to scaling and relabeling
rows.value: The model is identifiable up to ∼scale when σ > 2s.
rows.note: The theorem concerns the specified model class, with strict sparsity and a spark constraint; it is not an empirical test of trained SAE feature stability.
rows.check: The row is a theorem (Claim 5.2) about the abstract population model class Mspk(d,p;s,σ), re-deriving a classic dictionary-learning uniqueness result. It is not a measurement of SAE features in any network. It cannot show whether learned SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units of a model's representation, so it should not be linked to V5.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The population spark-constrained dictionary-learning model class with σ > 2s
reader_labels.reason: The paper proves identifiability up to scaling and relabeling in this setting (r1).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Application to ordinary or empirically trained SAEs
reader_labels.reason: The guarantee requires the specified spark-constrained model class; the paper says the relaxed SAE class lacks the same identifiability guarantees, and does not establish empirical SAE canonicity (r1).
